headline: Keep {arm:September}: both candidates cost about a quarter more per reply ({cost.uplift_range}) and neither keeps Kairo in character better.
lede: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} passes the character check {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs} points less often than {arm:September}, clearly worse, and {arm:1017} is not separated from it. Only a candidate that cost no more than {arm:September} could change the call; cost is measured, so the late and uncalibrated character judge cannot reverse it.

caveats.material_if: Only if a different character check, declared in advance, would have favoured a candidate; cost, the deciding finding, is measured and does not depend on the check.
Only if {arm:September} is not the model in production; every cost uplift and character change is read against it.
Only if the judge reads {arm:September}'s replies as in character more often than equally good candidate replies; even then no candidate is shown better, and cost, the deciding finding, is measured.
Only if a setting other than the served model also moved between arms and made the candidates cost more; cost, the deciding finding, would then belong partly to that setting.

decision.text: Keep {arm:September}, the control, for Kairo. It costs {cost_per_1k.September} per thousand replies, the least of the three, and no candidate holds character better.
{arm:qwen3.8-flash}: it costs {cost.uplift.qwen3.8-flash} more and passes the character check less often, a drop whose interval excludes zero.
{arm:1017}: it costs {cost.uplift.1017} more for a pass rate not separated from the control's ({reading.1017.interval} points), and the judge marks it out of character more often.

{arm:September} itself holds character in only {strata.off_lane.September.persona.holds_character.mean} of off-lane replies, its weakest place. The prior finding that {arm:qwen3.8-flash} lowers production cost is contradicted here: it costs {cost.uplift.qwen3.8-flash} more. Its worst plausible drop, {weakest.value} points, is the figure nearest the margin.
Find out why {arm:qwen3.8-flash} now costs more than the control before any further round on it; a candidate cheaper than {arm:September} is the only thing that would reopen the call.

claims.text: Both candidates cost more per reply than {arm:September}, and each gap is clear of zero.

evidence.caption: Production cost per thousand replies, with intervals; the candidates cost {cost.uplift_range} more than the control.

claims.text: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} passes the character check {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs} points less often than {arm:September}, clearly worse though within the {aspect.margin}-point margin; {arm:1017} is not separated from the control.

evidence.caption: Change in pass rate against the control, in points, at {reading.1017.level}; the shaded band is the declared margin. Two of {arm:qwen3.8-flash}'s trials were lost to the harness, so its rate counts slightly fewer trials.

claims.text: On the judge's holds-character verdict, both candidates are worse than {arm:September} after correction; {arm:1017} by {contrast.1017.persona.holds_character.delta|abs} points.

evidence.caption: Corrected contrasts against the control at {family.level}. {arm:1017} spent {reasoning_ratio.1017} of its output reasoning against the control's {reasoning_ratio.September}, so its loss may belong partly to its reasoning budget.

claims.text: Off-lane asks, where the user wants non-music help, carry about half of each candidate's holds-character loss ({strata.off_lane.loss_share.1017.persona.holds_character} for {arm:1017}).

evidence.caption: Holds-character rate minus the control's in the five largest strata, in points; uncorrected, so read as leads.

claims.text: Most kept off-lane failures show one pattern: the reply brushes off the non-music ask, then answers it anyway.

evidence.caption: Four kept cards from the stratum where the loss concentrates, out of {count.failures.character adherence (v2).qwen3.8-flash.off_lane} off-lane failures for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and {count.failures.character adherence (v2).1017.off_lane} for {arm:1017}.

explore.control: The margin a candidate may fall behind the control on the character check
explore.binds: Whether each candidate counts as no worse than the control
explore.outcome: The call holds at every margin. {arm:1017} counts as no worse above {flip_margin.1017} points and {arm:qwen3.8-flash} above {flip_margin.qwen3.8-flash}; neither changes the call, because both cost more.

omitted.what: The judge's ordinal outcome and transcript scores
omitted.why: They point the same way as the pass rate on an uncalibrated scale, and add nothing to the call.
Not separated for either candidate; it does not bear on the call.

omitted.what: Failed-reply notices, tool provider faults, turns over budget and items delivered
omitted.why: At or near zero for every arm; they do not separate the options.
Describes what the test cost to run, not what production would pay.

omitted.why: Too small to read; they stay in the full tables.

next.text: Reconcile {arm:qwen3.8-flash}'s cost with the earlier round that found it cheaper: compare the pricing and output length behind each.
next.settles: Whether it is cheaper than the control anywhere; if so, it becomes a priced tradeoff rather than a rejected option.

next.text: Re-run {arm:1017} with its reasoning budget set to match the control's share of output spent reasoning.
next.settles: Whether its holds-character loss belongs to the model or to its budget, and what it costs at that budget.

next.text: Tighten the directive to brush off non-music asks without answering them, and re-run the off-lane cases on all three models.
next.settles: Whether the largest share of the loss is a prompt issue every model shares, the control included.

next.text: Calibrate the judge against human ratings, starting with off-lane replies.
next.settles: Whether the judged character losses are real or a judge preference.

next.text: Declare the character check, the control and the margin before the next round runs.

method.text: {cases} conversations, each run {repeats} times per model; intervals count conversations, not repeats.
The campaign does not state what makes a trial pass on the character check; the pass rate counts trials marked passed over usable trials.

Readings against the control are at {reading.1017.level}. Contrasts are corrected together by Holm's method across {family.family_size} comparisons, each interval at {family.level}. Stratum breakdowns are uncorrected.
Character verdicts come from {judge.model}, with {judged.persona.holds_character.calibration_ratings} human calibration ratings.
Cost replicates what production would pay per reply, shown per thousand replies. No monthly volume was declared, so no monthly figure is given.
Whether the simulated user's request settings were the same on every run was not recorded.
Latency, input and output tokens and model call counts were not compared.
